editorial:
Ever wondered what it actually means to be a decent person in a world that feels like it is changing every five minutes? You get to go on that exact journey with director Bobby Roth. After becoming a grandfather, he starts questioning how to be a good role model for the next generation. Instead of reading a textbook, he just starts talking to people. He sits down with over fifty friends, both men and women, to get their honest takes on parenting, feminism, and the mistakes they have made. The vibe is very intimate and relaxed, feeling more like a long chat over coffee than a stiff movie. It feels like you are eavesdropping on real, raw conversations about life and love.

What really works here is the honesty. You will see people open up about things they usually keep hidden, which makes the pacing feel natural and rewarding. Some parts might feel a bit slow if you want high action, but the emotional payoff is huge. It is a great pick for anyone who likes deep conversations or is going through a life transition. If you can, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or you can rent it on Apple TV for a quiet night in. It is a thoughtful piece of film that stays with you long after the credits roll.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with Bobby reflecting on all the different answers he received. There is no single magic formula for being a good man, but he finds peace in the idea that being open to change and listening to others is the key. He concludes that goodness is a lifelong practice rather than a destination. The final scenes show him feeling more connected to his grandson and his friends, ending on a hopeful and warm note.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves real-life stories and deep conversations about growth.
